- agents-sdk: Build AI agents on Cloudflare Workers using the Agents SDK. Load when creating stateful agents, durable workflows, real-time WebSocket apps, scheduled tasks, MCP servers, chat applications, voice agents, or browser automation. Covers Agent class, state management, callable RPC, Workflows, durable execution, queues, retries, observability, and React hooks. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- cloudflare: Comprehensive Cloudflare platform skill covering Workers, Pages, storage (KV, D1, R2), AI (Workers AI, Vectorize, Agents SDK), feature flags (Flagship), networking (Tunnel, Spectrum), security (WAF, DDoS), and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi). Use for any Cloudflare development task. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- cloudflare-email-service: Send and receive transactional emails with Cloudflare Email Service (Email Sending + Email Routing). Use when building email sending (Workers binding or REST API), email routing, Agents SDK email handling, or integrating email into any app — Workers, Node.js, Python, Go, etc. Also use for email deliverability, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, wrangler email setup, MCP email tools, or when a coding agent needs to send emails. Even for simple requests like "add email to my Worker" — this skill has critical config details.
- durable-objects: Create and review Cloudflare Durable Objects. Use when building stateful coordination (chat rooms, multiplayer games, booking systems), implementing RPC methods, SQLite storage, alarms, WebSockets, or reviewing DO code for best practices. Covers Workers integration, wrangler config, and testing with Vitest. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- sandbox-sdk: Build sandboxed applications for secure code execution. Load when building AI code execution, code interpreters, CI/CD systems, interactive dev environments, or executing untrusted code. Covers Sandbox SDK lifecycle, commands, files, code interpreter, and preview URLs. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- steel-browser: Use this skill for any web task where WebFetch or curl would fail or be insufficient — pages that require JavaScript to render, forms to fill and submit, screenshots or PDFs of live pages, CAPTCHA/bot-protection bypass, login flows, and multi-step browser navigation with persistent session state. WebFetch returns empty HTML for JS-rendered pages; this skill runs a real cloud browser that executes JavaScript, maintains cookies, clicks buttons, and handles anti-bot measures. Trigger when the user wants you to actually perform a web task (visit, interact, extract, capture) rather than just write code for it. Skip only for: static pages a simple GET can fetch, localhost or private-network targets, writing browser automation code the user will run themselves, or conceptual questions about browser tools.
- turnstile-spin: Set up Cloudflare Turnstile end-to-end in a project — scan the codebase, create the widget via the Cloudflare API, deploy the managed siteverify Worker, write the frontend snippets, validate, and persist the skill. Load this when a user asks to add Turnstile, set up CAPTCHA, protect a form from bots, or fix a Turnstile integration. Mirrors developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/spin.
- web-perf: Analyzes web performance using Chrome DevTools MCP. Measures Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) and supplementary metrics (FCP, TBT, Speed Index), identifies render-blocking resources, network dependency chains, layout shifts, caching issues, and accessibility gaps. Use when asked to audit, profile, debug, or optimize page load performance, Lighthouse scores, or site speed. Biases towards retrieval from current documentation over pre-trained knowledge.
- workers-best-practices: Reviews and authors Cloudflare Workers code against production best practices. Load when writing new Workers, reviewing Worker code, configuring wrangler.jsonc, or checking for common Workers anti-patterns (streaming, floating promises, global state, secrets, bindings, observability). Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- wrangler: Cloudflare Workers CLI for deploying, developing, and managing Workers, KV, R2, D1, Vectorize, Hyperdrive, Workers AI, Containers, Queues, Workflows, Pipelines, and Secrets Store. Load before running wrangler commands to ensure correct syntax and best practices. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.
- leakage-review: Detect and block target leakage before training — scan column names for post-outcome signals, check timestamp ordering and feature availability at prediction time, and require explicit human approval to use any suspicious column. Load before proposing or launching experiments.
- model-card: Assemble a trustworthy, reproducible model card — objective, data, split, experiments, best vs baseline, risks, next steps, and a provenance footer. Load when writing the final report for a study.
- optuna-search: Run small, capped hyperparameter searches that tune on validation only — TPE sampler by default, pruning on, bounded trial budget, every trial's params and metrics logged. Load when a hypothesis calls for tuning a model family.
- tabular-ds-protocol: The non-negotiable protocol for a tabular ML study — deterministic split first, baseline before tuned models, document the target and metric, leakage review, compare to baseline, produce a model card. Load at the start of any Labmate study.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with high design quality. Use this skill when the user asks to build web components, pages, or applications. Generates creative, polished code that avoids generic AI aesthetics.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
Done. Here's what I did.

## What I cleaned up

I went through the whole cockpit (`apps/cockpit`) and stripped the decorative "avionics" layer that was working against a professional feel, while keeping the dark instrument identity and the panel/grid layout intact. The principle I applied: **reserve color and motion for meaning** (cyan = live, amber = caution, red = the agent caught bad science), and let the data lead instead of the chrome.

Removed / toned down:
- **Full-screen CRT scanline + film-grain overlay** — gone (the biggest "unprofessional" tell).
- **Graph-paper grid tiled across the background** — gone; flat surface now.
- **Per-panel "bezel screw" corner ticks** — removed.
- **`§01 / §02` section numbers** on every panel header — removed.
- **Looping scanline "sweep" on running cards** — replaced with a quiet static cyan edge.
- **Random-digit scramble on live metrics** — replaced with a calm, steady dimmed readout (the green lock-flash on settle is kept — that one *means* something).
- **Heavy neon glows** — softened the alert glow, the flag lamp, the timeline spine, and removed the dock's heavy drop shadow.
- **Typography** — dropped Orbitron + wide letter-spacing on panel titles (now a clean uppercase Archivo), tightened the brand and studies-title spacing, slightly smaller card titles and the big recommendation verb.
- **Corners** — radius 2px → 5px for a more modern, less industrial look.
- **Themey copy** — "ACQUIRING…" → real titles, "⚠ Signal lost" → "Connection lost", `[ + PROPOSE HYPOTHESIS ]` → "Propose a hypothesis to begin", "◉ acquiring…" → "running…".
- Deleted the now-dead CSS (unused vars, `.crt`, `.crosshair`, `sweep-down` keyframe).

Net: **8 files, ~144 deletions / 50 insertions** — mostly CSS removal.

## Verification
- `npm run build` (which runs `tsc --noEmit` with `noUnusedLocals`/`noUnusedParameters`, then `vite build`) passes clean.
- Grepped to confirm no removed class/variable is still referenced anywhere.
- I did **not** get a live screenshot: the app reads from a backend at `localhost:4010` with no fixture/mock mode, so rendering it would mean standing up the whole Cloudflare control plane — out of scope for a presentational pass. The changes are CSS + declarative copy, so the green build is the meaningful check.

I kept the "LABMATE ▸ MISSION CONTROL" brand and the single large recommendation verb as deliberate focal points — tell me if you'd rather neutralize those too.

The work is isolated on branch **`worktree-ui-cleanup2`** (worktree at `.claude/worktrees/ui-cleanup2`), not committed or merged. To eyeball it: `cd` into that worktree's `apps/cockpit` and `npm run dev` against your usual backend.

===== GOAL_E2E.md =====
# Goal — end-to-end: Managed Agent runs real experiments, human steers from the UI

This is the demo. A user gives a problem and a dataset in the cockpit; the backend
spins up an **Anthropic Managed Agent** (real API) with custom tools, MCP, and the
DS skills; the agent proposes experiments that **run in Modal sandboxes** (real);
the agent **reviews the results and loops**; and the cockpit is how the human
watches it happen, suggests changes mid-flight, and gets back the final report and
model.

It builds directly on what you already have (the control plane, the MCP tool
surface, the Modal runner, the cockpit). The **one new component** is the
*agent runtime* — the bridge that runs a Managed Agents session, catches the
agent's custom-tool calls on the event stream, executes them against Modal and
your control plane, and feeds results back.

> Read this whole file, then paste the **Brief** into Claude Code, then the
> **/goal**. The slices at the end are the suggested order; let Claude sequence
> within them.

---

## 0. How Managed Agents actually works (grounding — don't skip)

Verified against the current docs (beta `managed-agents-2026-04-01`). The mental
model that matters for our loop:

- You create **three persisted resources**, in order:
  1. an **Agent** — model, system prompt, **tools**, **mcp_servers**, **skills**
     (these live on the *agent*, not the session). Versioned; sessions pin a version.
  2. an **Environment** — a cloud sandbox config (`config.type: "cloud"`,
     networking). This is *Anthropic's* sandbox where the agent's built-in tools
     (bash, files, code) run.
  3. a **Session** — references one agent + one environment, holds conversation
     state as an **event stream** that outlives the context window.
- You **drive work by sending events** (`user.message`) and **observe by streaming
  events** back (SSE via `sessions.events.stream()`).
- **Custom tools are the integration seam.** When the agent decides to use a tool
  *you* defined (e.g. `launch_experiment`), it emits a tool-use event and the
  session pauses for that tool; you execute it on your own infra and return a
  `user.custom_tool_result` event (`custom_tool_use_id`, `content`, `is_error`).
  **This is how the agent reaches Modal** without us handing it arbitrary compute.
- **MCP servers** attach on the agent; **vaults** (`vault_ids` at session create)
  hold any MCP OAuth/bearer creds, refreshed by Anthropic.
- **Outcomes** (define a success rubric the agent self-evaluates against) is a
  research-preview feature behind an access request. **Design for it, but gate it**
  — our fallback "done" is our own `/api/grade` against `docs/rubric.json`, which
  needs no preview access.
- Headers: every call needs the beta header; the SDK adds it automatically for
  `client.beta.{agents,environments,sessions,vaults}.*`. Set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

Key constraint to honor in the design: **agents have no delete, only archive, and
archive is permanent** — so the runtime should *reuse* a small number of agents/
environments (created once, by version), not create-per-study.

Primary references (fetch if you need detail):
- Overview: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview
- Quickstart: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/quickstart
- Sessions: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions
- Event stream: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming
- Tools: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/tools
- MCP connector: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector
- Define outcomes: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes
- Endpoint reference: https://github.com/anthropics/skills/blob/main/skills/claude-api/shared/managed-agents-api-reference.md

---

## 1. Target architecture (what "joined up" means here)

```
  Cockpit (apps/cockpit)
    │  POST /api/studies        (problem + dataset upload)
    │  GET  /api/studies/{id}   (poll the ledger)
    │  GET  /api/studies/{id}/stream   (SSE: live agent activity)
    │  POST /api/feedback       (human "suggest changes" mid-run)
    ▼
  Control plane (apps/web — Cloudflare Worker, D1, R2, DO)
    │  on study create: enqueue a "start agent" job  ─────────────┐
    │  proxies the agent runtime's event stream to the cockpit    │
    ▼                                                              │
  Agent runtime (apps/agent-runtime — NEW)         ◀──────────────┘
    │  1. ensure Agent + Environment exist (once, versioned)
    │  2. sessions.create(agent, environment) for this study
    │  3. send user.message: the brief + data contract + rubric
    │  4. sessions.events.stream():
    │       • text/thinking  → forward to control plane → cockpit
    │       • custom tool-use → DISPATCH (below) → custom_tool_result
    │       • idle/awaiting   → check done; if not, nudge next step
    │  5. on done: pull report+model, mark study complete
    │
    │   custom tool dispatch (the agent's "hands"):
    │     propose_experiments → write hypotheses to control plane
    │     launch_experiment   → POST Modal runner (REAL) → record run
    │     query_runs          → read ledger
    │     record_critique     → write critique/decision
    │     write_report        → render model card → R2
    ▼
  Modal runner (apps/modal-runner — REAL sklearn/optuna jobs)
```

Two services already speak HTTP over your OpenAPI contract; the agent runtime is a
long-lived Node (or Python) process that holds the SSE stream. It can run on Modal
itself (a `modal.App` with a web endpoint + a long-running function) so you don't
need a separate host at the hackathon.

### Where the agent's tools come from
The agent's **custom tools** mirror your existing MCP tool surface — same names,
same JSON shapes from `apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml`. You can wire them two ways;
do **(a)** for the demo and leave (b) as a note:
- **(a) Custom tools handled by the runtime.** Declare them on the agent as custom
  tools; the runtime catches each tool-use on the stream and executes it. Full
  control, easy to log, no extra hop. **Use this.**
- **(b) MCP server.** Point the agent's `mcp_servers` at your deployed
  `apps/mcp-server`. Cleaner separation, but adds an auth/tunnel surface. Optional.

---

## 2. Brief (paste this into Claude Code first)

```
You are extending Labmate to a real end-to-end demo. Today it has a Cloudflare
control plane (apps/web), an MCP tool surface + OpenAPI contract
(apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml), a Modal experiment runner (apps/modal-runner), and a
cockpit (apps/cockpit). They are joined up over the contract.

Build the missing piece and wire the loop with REAL API usage:

GOAL OF THE DEMO: a user enters a problem + uploads a dataset in the cockpit; the
backend starts an Anthropic Managed Agent (real, beta managed-agents-2026-04-01)
whose tools/MCP/skills let it propose experiments; experiments run for real in
Modal sandboxes; the agent reviews results and iterates; the cockpit streams what's
happening, lets the human suggest changes mid-run, and shows the final report+model.

Read first, in this order:
  - docs/GOAL_E2E.md            (this plan — architecture + the loop + slices)
  - apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml  (the contract every tool call conforms to)
  - apps/agent-runtime/         (NEW — the scaffold to flesh out; start at README.md)
  - apps/modal-runner/runner.py (the real executor your launch_experiment calls)
  - docs/data_contract.md, docs/metric_contract.md, docs/rubric.json

Hard rules (unchanged, enforced):
  1. The agent never runs arbitrary training code. It calls the custom tool
     launch_experiment with a manifest; the Modal runner is the only executor and
     rejects manifests with banned columns in features or tune_on=test.
  2. Every run links to a hypothesis and carries rationale + provenance
     (dataset_hash, code_hash, seed). Every critique and decision is recorded.
  3. Compute is gated: launch_experiment requires a recorded approval; without one
     it returns 402 and the runtime surfaces an approval request to the cockpit.
  4. Managed Agents resources: reuse a versioned agent + environment created by a
     bootstrap script — do NOT create-per-study (archive is permanent, no delete).
  5. Use real keys from .env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MODAL_*, CLOUDFLARE_*). Never
     invent credentials; if a key is missing, stop and say which one.

Definition of done is machine-checkable (see the /goal). Outcomes (agent self-eval
rubric) is research-preview — design for it but gate behind MANAGED_AGENTS_OUTCOMES
and fall back to POST /api/grade against docs/rubric.json, which needs no preview.

Prove it with apps/agent-runtime/tests/e2e.smoke.test.* : with a stubbed Anthropic
+ stubbed Modal it must drive create-study → propose → launch → record → critique →
report end to end, asserting the ledger has a baseline run, >=1 corrected rerun, and
a report artifact. Then run the same path once against the REAL APIs for the demo.
```

---

## 3. /goal (paste after the brief)

```
/goal Wire Labmate end to end: a problem+dataset submitted in the cockpit drives a
real Anthropic Managed Agents session whose custom tools run experiments in Modal,
review results, and loop, with the human steering from the cockpit.

Done means ALL of the following are true and verifiable:
  - apps/agent-runtime exists and exposes: POST /agent/start {study_id} and
    GET /agent/{study_id}/stream (SSE). A bootstrap script creates ONE versioned
    agent (model claude-opus-4-8, the DS system prompt, the Labmate custom tools,
    the tabular-ds/leakage/optuna/model-card skills) and ONE cloud environment, and

  - Creating a study via POST /api/studies triggers /agent/start, which calls
    sessions.create(agent, environment), sends the brief+data-contract+rubric as a
    user.message, and streams events.
  - The runtime dispatches the agent's custom tool-use events to real handlers:
    propose_experiments, launch_experiment (REAL POST to the Modal runner),
    query_runs, record_critique, write_report — returning user.custom_tool_result
    each time, and persisting everything to the control plane over the OpenAPI
    contract.
  - launch_experiment enforces the approval gate (402 without one) and the runner
    rejects banned-column/tune_on=test manifests (422).
  - The cockpit, on a live study, shows streaming agent activity, a working
    "suggest changes" box that injects a user.message into the session, the run
    table updating as Modal jobs finish, and a final report+model link.
  - The loop self-corrects at least once: the agent (or the leakage/critique tool)
    catches the planted leakage or a test-set-tuning attempt and reruns corrected.
  - apps/agent-runtime/tests/e2e.smoke.test.* passes against stubbed Anthropic+Modal,
    npm run guard is green, and POST /api/grade returns verdict=done for the demo
    study (caught_an_issue check passes).
  - A one-command demo (npm run demo:e2e) runs the whole path on the SEEDED study

```

===== GOAL_E2E.md (rest) =====
---

## 4. Suggested slices (order of build)

**Slice A — agent runtime skeleton + bootstrap (get a session talking).**
Flesh out `apps/agent-runtime`. Implement `bootstrap.mjs`: create the versioned
agent (custom tools declared from the OpenAPI shapes) + the cloud environment,
print/save their IDs. Implement `POST /agent/start` to `sessions.create` and send a
first `user.message`, and `sessions.events.stream()` logging every event. Success:
`node bootstrap.mjs` then starting a session makes the agent respond and call at
least one custom tool you can see on the stream.

**Slice B — custom tool dispatch (give the agent hands).**
Implement the dispatcher: map each custom tool-use to a handler that calls the
control plane / Modal over the contract, then send `user.custom_tool_result`.
Start with `propose_experiments` and `query_runs` (cheap, no compute), then
`launch_experiment` against the **real** Modal runner with the approval gate.
Success: the agent proposes hypotheses and launches one real Modal run that lands
in the ledger with metrics + provenance.

**Slice C — the review loop + done.**
Wire `record_critique`/decision and `write_report`. On each idle/awaiting-input
event, the runtime checks done: if outcomes preview is enabled, read its verdict;
else call `/api/grade`. If not done and budget remains, nudge the agent
("review the latest runs; propose the next experiment or stop"). Seed the leakage/
test-set-tuning catch so the loop self-corrects once. Success: a study runs
baseline → several experiments → a caught issue → corrected rerun → report, and
`/api/grade` returns done.

**Slice D — cockpit live view + steering.**
In `apps/cockpit`: subscribe to `GET /api/studies/{id}/stream` (the control plane
proxies the runtime's SSE) and render the activity timeline into the evidence
ledger pane; make the "suggest changes" box POST feedback that the runtime injects
as a `user.message`; show the report+model link when complete. Success: you can
watch a run live and change its course from the UI.

**Slice E — make it demo-proof.**
`npm run demo:e2e` runs the seeded study deterministically; loading/empty/running
states everywhere; archive nothing by accident; record the self-correction moment.
Success: it runs clean twice in a row.

---

## 5. What to show the judges

1. Type a real problem + drop a CSV in the cockpit. **(Impact + Demo)**
2. The agent spins up, profiles, and proposes experiments — visible live. **(Demo)**
3. A Modal job runs for real; the run appears in the ledger with metrics. **(Demo)**
4. The agent flags the planted leakage / test-set tuning and **reruns corrected**
   — the money moment. **(Demo + Orchestration)**
5. You inject "recall matters more than precision, keep FPR ≤ 20%" from the box and

node apply-e2e.mjs

# 3. wire it up

===== agent-runtime/README =====
# Labmate agent runtime

The bridge between an Anthropic **Managed Agents** session and Labmate's own infra
(the Cloudflare control plane + the Modal experiment runner). This is the piece
that turns "an agent that can talk" into "an agent that runs real experiments and
reviews them in a loop while a human steers from the cockpit."

Grounded in the current Managed Agents beta (`managed-agents-2026-04-01`). See
`docs/GOAL_E2E.md` §0 for the verified mental model and doc links.

## What it does

1. **Bootstrap (once):** create ONE versioned **agent** (model `claude-opus-4-8`,
   the DS system prompt, the Labmate **custom tools**, the DS **skills**) and ONE
   cloud **environment**; save their IDs to `.env`. Agents can't be deleted (only
   archived, permanently), so we reuse them — never create-per-study.
2. **Start a session per study:** `sessions.create(agent, environment)`, then send
   the brief + data contract + rubric as a `user.message`.
3. **Hold the event stream:** `sessions.events.stream()`. For each event:
   - text / thinking → forward to the control plane → cockpit (live activity);
   - **custom tool-use → dispatch** to a real handler, return `user.custom_tool_result`;
   - idle / awaiting input → check "done"; if not, nudge the next step.
4. **Custom tool dispatch is the agent's hands:**
   `propose_experiments`, `launch_experiment` (REAL Modal call), `query_runs`,
   `record_critique`, `write_report` — all persisted over the OpenAPI contract.
5. **Done:** if the Outcomes preview is enabled, read its verdict; otherwise call
   `POST /api/grade` against `docs/rubric.json`.

```
POST /agent/start {study_id}          → create session, send brief, start streaming
GET  /agent/{study_id}/stream  (SSE)  → live agent events (control plane proxies to cockpit)
POST /agent/{study_id}/message        → inject a human "suggest changes" message
```

## Files

- `src/anthropic.mjs` — thin SDK wrapper (sets the beta, exposes agents/env/sessions/events).
- `src/bootstrap.mjs` — create the agent + environment, write IDs to `.env`.
- `src/tools.mjs` — the custom-tool *definitions* (names + JSON schemas, from the
  OpenAPI contract) the agent is given.
- `src/dispatch.mjs` — maps each tool-use to a real handler (control plane / Modal).
- `src/loop.mjs` — the session lifecycle: start, stream, dispatch, nudge, finish.
- `src/server.mjs` — the HTTP/SSE surface above.
- `src/config.mjs` — env loading + required-key checks.
- `tests/e2e.smoke.test.mjs` — drives the whole loop with Anthropic + Modal stubbed.

## Run

```bash
# 0. deps (uses the official SDK)
npm install

# 1. one-time: create the agent + environment, save IDs to .env
node src/bootstrap.mjs

# 2. start the runtime
node src/server.mjs        # listens on AGENT_RUNTIME_PORT (default 8betaY)

# 3. smoke test (no real API calls)
npm test

# 4. the deterministic demo against real APIs
npm run demo:e2e           # from repo root
```

> The runtime can also be deployed as a Modal app (a web endpoint + a long-running
> function holding the stream) so you don't need a separate host at the hackathon.
> See `src/server.mjs` for the note.

===== package.json (root) workspaces+scripts =====
workspaces: ["packages/*","apps/web","apps/mcp-server","apps/agent-runtime"]
scripts: {
 "setup": "node scripts/setup.mjs",
 "preflight": "bash scripts/preflight.sh",
 "gen:data": "python3 scripts/gen_dataset.py",
 "schema:check": "node scripts/schema-check.mjs",
 "lint": "eslint . --max-warnings=0",
 "lint:fix": "eslint . --fix",
 "format": "prettier --write \"**/*.{js,mjs,json,md}\"",
 "format:check": "prettier --check \"**/*.{js,mjs,json,md}\"",
 "test": "node --test tests/*.test.mjs",
 "py:check": "cd apps/modal-runner && ruff check . && (mypy runner.py || true)",
 "py:test": "cd apps/modal-runner && pytest -q",
 "dev:mcp": "npm run dev --workspace=apps/mcp-server",
 "dev:web": "cd apps/web && npx wrangler dev",
 "db:migrate": "cd apps/web && npx wrangler d1 execute labmate --file=./schema.sql",
 "study": "node .claude/workflows/run-study.js examples/sla_tickets",
 "grade": "python3 scripts/grade_study.py --rubric docs/rubric.json",
 "guard": "npm run schema:check && npm run lint && npm run test && npm run test:agent",
 "guard:full": "npm run guard && npm run py:check && npm run py:test",
 "spec:lint": "npx @redocly/cli lint apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml",
 "spec:mock": "npx @stoplight/prism-cli mock apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml --port 4010",
 "spec:types": "npx openapi-typescript apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml -o packages/api-types/index.ts",
 "spec:docs": "npx @redocly/cli build-docs apps/api-spec/openapi.yaml -o apps/api-spec/index.html",
 "agent:bootstrap": "node apps/agent-runtime/src/bootstrap.mjs",
 "agent:dev": "node apps/agent-runtime/src/server.mjs",
 "test:agent": "node --test apps/agent-runtime/tests/*.test.mjs",
 "demo:e2e": "node scripts/demo_e2e.mjs"
}

===== web src tree =====
apps/web/src/worker.js
apps/web/src/grade.js
apps/web/src/profiles.js

===== wrangler.toml =====
name = "labmate"
main = "src/worker.js"
compatibility_date = "2025-01-01"
compatibility_flags = ["nodejs_compat"]

# schema.sql is imported as a Text module so the Worker can self-apply the ledger
# schema on first request (in addition to `wrangler d1 execute --file=./schema.sql`).
[[rules]]
type = "Text"
globs = ["**/*.sql"]
fallthrough = true

# ---- D1 (studies, hypotheses, runs, feedback, critiques, decisions, artifacts) ----
# Create with: npx wrangler d1 create labmate
# then paste the printed database_id here AND into .env (CLOUDFLARE_D1_DATABASE_ID).
# The placeholder below is fine for `wrangler dev` (local mode keys storage by binding).
[[d1_databases]]
binding = "DB"
database_name = "labmate"
database_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"

# ---- R2 (artifacts, reports, model files) ----
# Create with: npx wrangler r2 bucket create labmate-artifacts
[[r2_buckets]]
binding = "ARTIFACTS"
bucket_name = "labmate-artifacts"

# ---- Durable Object (live study state / event stream for the cockpit) ----
[[durable_objects.bindings]]
name = "STUDY"
class_name = "StudySession"

[[migrations]]
tag = "v1"
new_classes = ["StudySession"]

# ---- Vars / secrets ----
# LABMATE_INTERNAL_TOKEN is a secret: set with `npx wrangler secret put LABMATE_INTERNAL_TOKEN`
# (or apps/web/.dev.vars locally). MODAL_RUNNER_URL is the deployed runner endpoint.
[vars]
LABMATE_ENV = "dev"
MODAL_RUNNER_URL = ""

   - Runtime: `POST /api/experiments/propose` → control plane persists them by `hypothesis_id`
   - Returns: hypothesis IDs the agent can reference

   - Cockpit user can approve in UI, or the agent waits (for demo, auto-approve within budget is baked in)
   - Returns: `approval_id`

   - Runtime:

     - `POST /api/experiments/launch` → control plane forwards to Modal runner (real HTTPS call)

     - Agent sees the error, corrects manifest, reruns — this drives **the self-correction moment**

   - Runtime: `POST /api/reports` → control plane assembles the model card, writes to R2
   - Returns: `{ uri, compares_best_to_baseline: true, ... }`

## 5. GAPS & CONTRADICTIONS WITH COMMITTED ARCHITECTURE

**The Committed Architecture (CLAUDE.md):**
- Describes **multi-agent orchestration**: ds-planner, experiment-runner, experiment-critic, report-writer subagents
- Describes MCP tool surface: `create_study`, `profile_dataset`, `launch_experiment`, `record_human_feedback`, `write_report`, `grade_study_against_rubric`
- Describes a **run-study.js driver** (`.claude/workflows/run-study.js`) that calls these tools sequentially
- Assumes **Claude Code runs the loop**, not a managed agent

**The E2E Overlay:**
- Replaces the multi-agent orchestration with **ONE Managed Agent** (Anthropic-hosted, real API)
- Replaces the MCP tool surface with **custom tools** (same names, same JSON shapes, but dispatched by the runtime, not by Claude Code)
- Replaces run-study.js with **apps/agent-runtime** (a Node.js bridge that holds the event stream and dispatches)
- The agent (not Claude Code) runs the loop autonomously

**Key Contradictions:**

1. **Tool Interface:** CLAUDE.md says Claude Code calls MCP tools; E2E overlay says the Managed Agent calls custom tools. They're semantically equivalent (same names, same shapes), but:
   - MCP tools are endpoints the MCP server exposes
   - Custom tools are tool definitions sent to the Managed Agents API

## 5. GAPS & CONTRADICTIONS WITH COMMITTED ARCHITECTURE

**The Committed Architecture (CLAUDE.md):**
- Describes **multi-agent orchestration**: ds-planner, experiment-runner, experiment-critic, report-writer subagents
- Describes MCP tool surface: `create_study`, `profile_dataset`, `launch_experiment`, `record_human_feedback`, `write_report`, `grade_study_against_rubric`
- Describes a **run-study.js driver** (`.claude/workflows/run-study.js`) that calls these tools sequentially
- Assumes **Claude Code runs the loop**, not a managed agent

**The E2E Overlay:**
- Replaces the multi-agent orchestration with **ONE Managed Agent** (Anthropic-hosted, real API)
- Replaces the MCP tool surface with **custom tools** (same names, same JSON shapes, but dispatched by the runtime, not by Claude Code)
- Replaces run-study.js with **apps/agent-runtime** (a Node.js bridge that holds the event stream and dispatches)
- The agent (not Claude Code) runs the loop autonomously

**Key Contradictions:**

1. **Tool Interface:** CLAUDE.md says Claude Code calls MCP tools; E2E overlay says the Managed Agent calls custom tools. They're semantically equivalent (same names, same shapes), but:
   - MCP tools are endpoints the MCP server exposes
   - Custom tools are tool definitions sent to the Managed Agents API
   - The runtime (not Claude) intercepts and executes them

   **Resolution:** The MCP server still exists; the control plane still handles the routes. The runtime just dispatches without going through MCP (option (a) from GOAL_E2E.md §1).

2. **Session Ownership:** CLAUDE.md implies Claude Code drives the loop (synchronous); E2E overlay has the Managed Agent drive it (asynchronous, long-lived session).
   - run-study.js makes sequential API calls
   - agent-runtime streams events and nudges the agent
   - **No conflict:** they're alternative execution modes for the same control plane

3. **Approval Flow:**
   - CLAUDE.md: `request_approval` returns an approval ID; the tool is a gate
   - E2E overlay: same, but the agent *can* call it without waiting (control plane may auto-approve in demo)
   - **No conflict:** same contract

4. **Critique Recording:**
   - CLAUDE.md: `record_human_feedback` (or similar) in MCP
   - E2E overlay: `record_critique` custom tool, new route `/api/critiques`
   - **Slight mismatch:** names differ (human_feedback vs critique), but semantic is the same
   - **Fix needed:** Either rename the tool or make the route name match

5. **Report Writing:**

1. Ingested via a new POST /api/datasets/upload endpoint (multipart form data).
2. Stored in R2 with a content-hash key.
3. Profiled live by scanning the CSV (row count, dtypes, missing %, leakage detection).
4. Its R2 key injected into every experiment manifest.

## 4. Human-Approval Gate

**Where it lives**:
- No hooks in `.claude/settings.json` (lines 1-20 show only advisory PreToolUse and Stop hooks that never block).

**Gating is implicit in run-study.js**: The script calls `request_approval` (line 103), then immediately calls `record_human_feedback` (line 109) to auto-approve. In production, a human would check the cockpit UI and manually POST the approval feedback before launches proceed.

## 5. Question/Brief Maps to create_study

A "question/brief" becomes:
- `brief`: Free-text business objective (e.g., "Predict SLA breach on support tickets so we can intervene early").
- `task_type`: "binary_classification" or "regression".
- `dataset_id`: Identifier (e.g., "sla_tickets").

- `budget`: max_trials and budget_seconds.

## LABMATE COCKPIT: COMPREHENSIVE UI REVIEW

Based on my complete exploration of `/Users/vincent/Documents/code/Labmate/apps/cockpit/src`, here are my detailed findings organized by your four questions:

### 1. ROUTING MODEL & UPLOAD ENTRY POINT

**Current Routing Architecture** (`/src/lib/router.ts:1-34`):
The cockpit uses a minimal dependency-free hash router with exactly two routes:
- `#/` → Study list view (StudyList.tsx)
- `#/study/{id}` → Study detail view (StudyDetail.tsx)

The route is parsed from `window.location.hash` and keyed as `{name: 'study', id}` or `{name: 'list'}`. No Create/Upload endpoint exists today.

**Current Study Creation Model**:
Line 67 in StudyList.tsx explicitly states: `<EmptyState label="No studies — create one via the MCP create_study tool" />`. All study creation flows through MCP tools only. There is **zero UI for importing data or initializing a study**.

**Recommended Upload + Ask-Question Entry Screen**:

The cleanest slot for a "New Study" flow would be a **third route** `#/create` that sits **between** the list and detail views:

```
New route pattern:
  #/                     → StudyList (unchanged, add a CTA button for "New Study")
  #/create               → CreateStudyModal (new: upload CSV + inline question editor)
  #/study/{id}           → StudyDetail (unchanged)
```

This would need:
- **CreateStudyPane.tsx**: Form with file input (CSV upload), text field for "Ask a question" + optional metadata (target, task_type, metric). 
- **API client method** (api/client.ts): `createStudy(manifest: {dataset_file: File; question: string; target?: string; ...})` → POST /api/studies with multipart/form-data
- **Hook in api/hooks.ts**: `useCreateStudy()` mutation with optimistic study creation, navigating on success to #/study/{id}

The UI would:
- Live in a **full-screen modal** or a **dedicated pane** (visual consistency with the cockpit glass aesthetic suggests modal for prominence)
- Use the existing Dock-style recommendation frame (`.rec` / `.feedback` patterns in styles.css:1215-1280) for the form layout
- Hook `navigate({name: 'study', id: newStudyId})` on success to immediately land in the detail view

**Why here?** 
- Keeps routing orthogonal (list → create modal → detail, no modal nesting)
- The list already has space for a floating CTA or header button
- Avoids polluting the StudyDetail component with an "init" state

---

### 2. DATA-FETCH LAYER & MISSING MUTATIONS

**Existing Query/Mutation Architecture** (`api/hooks.ts:1-230`):

The hooks follow a clean TanStack Query pattern:
- **Reads** (cached + live polled): `useStudies()`, `useStudy(id)` with live polling at 4s intervals when `isActiveStatus(run.status)` is true (line 35)
- **Writes** (optimistic overlay + toast): `approve`, `deny`, `rerun`, `banColumn`, `sendFeedback`, `generateReport`, `checkDone` (lines 59-226)

**Polling Logic** (line 35):
```typescript
refetchInterval: (query) => (hasActiveRun(query.state.data) ? 4000 : false),
```
This is intelligent—it only polls while a run is actively computing, then stops.

**Missing Mutations for Upload + Question Flow**:

Your new flow would require:
1. **`createStudy(params: {csv_file: File; question: string; target?: string; task_type?: string; metric?: string}) → Study`**
   - POST to a new endpoint (e.g., `/api/studies` with multipart form data)
   - On success, optimistically dispatch overlay action or just navigate (no existing data to merge)
   - Toast feedback: "Study created — initializing…"

2. **`uploadDataset(studyId: string, file: File) → DatasetVersion`** (optional, if you want mid-study re-upload)
   - Refreshes the data-contract pane on success
   - Would invalidate `qk.study(studyId)` to force re-fetch

3. **`askFollowUp(studyId: string, question: string) → Feedback`** (if you want a lightweight "refinement" flow)
   - Essentially a specialized `sendFeedback()` with a different scope or type

The existing `sendFeedback` hook (lines 176-203) already covers recording judgment as natural language, so the upload flow would piggyback on that.

**What's NOT missing**: The core study-editing mutations all exist. The gap is purely around *creation* and *onboarding*.

---

### 3. CONCRETE UI REFINEMENT OPPORTUNITIES (8-15 items beyond the declutter)

Having reviewed the current post-declutter state (CRT overlay still rendered but invisible, grid background present, corner ticks removed in recent pass, glows softened, 5px radius), here are actionable polish opportunities:

#### **Layout & Density**

1. **Panel headers (.panel__head:351-357, styles.css)** — The section numbers (§01, §02, etc.) feel decorative. Consider **discretionary grid lines** (hairline separator) between sections instead of section numbers, or relocate numbers to a small top-left bevel screw that echoes the panel aesthetic. Line too tall at 20px leading.

2. **Cockpit grid responsiveness (styles.css:1543-1555)** — The breakpoint at 1279px is jarring. At 1024px (iPad Pro landscape), the 12-col grid collapses to a single column. **Add intermediate breakpoint** at ~1024px with a 2-column layout (brief+contract on left, cards+runs stacked on right, ledger below) to improve tablet UX without full mobile reflow.

3. **Dock height is inflexible (--dock-h: 104px:63)** — On narrow viewports (<720px), the recommendation verb and feedback box stack vertically, but the fixed 104px minimum leaves wasted space. **Make dock height responsive**: 104px on ≥1280px, 140px on 720-1280px, 180px on mobile (giving textarea more breathing room).

4. **Toast positioning (styles.css:1386-1395)** — Fixed bottom-right at `calc(var(--dock-h) + 16px)` overlaps on small screens. **Reposition to top-right** (20px top, 20px right) or use a conditional offset that respects viewport height. Also, max-width: 360px is too wide on phones.

#### **Empty & Loading States**

5. **Empty states are inconsistent** (primitives.tsx:68-77, styles.css:593-619). The `.empty` container is flexbox-centered but doesn't scale icon sizes or provide visual hierarchy. **Add optional icon/glyph parameter** to `EmptyState` component, and size it relative to viewport (clamp(40px, 10vw, 120px)). Flatline SVG (styles.css:646-650) is too faint at opacity 0.4—boost to 0.6 on light/dark themes.

6. **Skeleton rows (primitives.tsx:96-108, styles.css:570-591)** — The `shimmer` animation is subtle but doesn't feel "acquiring". **Boost the shimmer gradient opacity** (from background-color-derived to explicit rgba). Also, SkeletonRows currently hardcodes row widths (38%, 24%, flex). **Make widths configurable** per pane to match actual layout (e.g., table rows should have equal-width columns).

#### **Data Display & Tables**

7. **Run table alignment (RunTable.tsx, styles.css:771-840)** — The metrics column shows up to 3 metrics but uses flex gap, which breaks alignment across rows. **Use CSS Grid with 3 equal columns** for the metrics sub-table, or right-align numbers consistently (tabular-nums already applied at .mono:145). Consider a **small "copy to clipboard" affordance** on run IDs (`.run-id:87`) for power users.

8. **Column table striping (styles.css:794-805)** — Leaky rows use `is-leaky` class with a faint red background and left inset shadow. **Make the background gradient subtle** (rotate from transparent to red at 45°) to add visual depth without harshness. Also, the shadow is 2px but the table padding is 8px—**increase shadow to 3px** to align with the gutter.

9. **Evidence ledger timeline color coding (styles.css:1086-1143)** — The gradient line (::before) and node colors are hardcoded to cyan. **Make node colors respect the entry type** (run → st-running, critique → crit-color, decision → decision-color, feedback → amber). The timeline spine should **use a subtle gradient** through the entry colors, or stay neutral with low opacity.

#### **Chips, Typography & Consistency**

10. **Chip padding inconsistency (styles.css:412-450)** — `.chip` is 2px/7px (very tight), `.tag-chip` is 1px/5px (even tighter), `.ban-btn` is 2px/7px. **Normalize to 4px vertical / 8px horizontal** across all small controls. Also, `.chip--struck` (text-decoration: line-through) doesn't change background—**add a subtle opacity or background tint** to visually "disable" it.

11. **Typography scale is rigid** — Font sizes jump from `--fs-micro: 0.6875rem` to `--fs-body: 0.8125rem` to `--fs-card-title: 1.25rem`. There's no `--fs-small: 0.75rem` for sub-labels. **Add intermediate sizes** (sm: 0.75, xs: 0.6rem) and use them in `.label`, `.parse-hint`, `.tl-entry__type` for better visual hierarchy. Line-height also doesn't scale (all 1.4)—**increase to 1.5 for body, 1.2 for headers**.

12. **Feedback chips animation (styles.css:1265-1273)** — The `cyanflash` animation is undefined in the provided CSS (only `pulse`, `breathe`, `blink`, `shimmer`, `typein`, `toastin`, `indeterminate`, `bloom` are defined). **Add `@keyframes cyanflash`**: `0% { box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--cyan); } 100% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 transparent; }` to give visual feedback when NL constraints are parsed.

#### **Accessibility & Interactive Feedback**

13. **Focus indicators on nested elements (styles.css:1461-1479)** — The `.seg:focus-visible` uses `outline-offset: -2px`, which insets the ring. **Make inset vs. outset consistent**: all buttons should use outset by default, except segmented controls (which should have a subtle background highlight instead of a ring). Also, `.seg--on-approve` and `.seg--on-deny` have inverted colors—ensure they still meet WCAG AA contrast (currently not verifiable from CSS alone).

14. **Lamp status indicator animation (styles.css:262-285)** — The `.lamp--running` pulses, but `.lamp--flag` has a bloom animation. **Unify to a single animation** (pulse works; bloom is ornamental). Also, the flag lamp uses `box-shadow: 0 0 14px var(--alert-glow)` but glow is `rgba(255, 77, 94, 0.45)`—**reduce opacity to 0.25** to avoid oversaturation on dark themes.

#### **Long-Running / Live Update UX**

15. **Live hairline progress indicator (styles.css:111-131)** — The `.live-hairline` animates when `computing && <div class="live-hairline" />` (StudyDetail.tsx:43). The indeterminate bar is slick, but there's **no visual feedback on how much time has elapsed**. Consider **adding a micro-progress** (% of budgetSeconds used) or replacing with a **color-shift animation** (cyan → amber as time progresses toward budget limit). Also, 2px height is barely visible at typical screen distance—**increase to 3px** or use a subtle glow.

---

### 4. LIVE UPDATE MECHANICS & TRIGGERED STUDY SURFACING

**Polling Strategy** (api/hooks.ts:22-37):

```typescript
useStudy(id): {
  refetchInterval: (query) => (hasActiveRun(query.state.data) ? 4000 : false),
}
```

- **4000ms interval** is conservative (4s between polls). For a live "triggered" study (e.g., user clicks "Run experiment"), this means **up to 4s latency** before the UI reflects the run's queued state.
- **Stops polling** once all runs exit active status (queued/running → completed/failed/stopped).
- **No WebSocket** or Server-Sent Events—purely HTTP polling.

**Optimistic Overlay** (state/overlay.tsx:1-126):

When a user clicks "Approve", the mutation:
1. Calls `api.requestApproval()` (hits the real POST)
2. **Immediately** calls `dispatch({t: 'hyp', status: 'approved'})` (optimistic)
3. Merges overlay onto StudyDetail (mergeStudyDetail:114-125), so the card flips to approved before server confirms
4. On success, shows toast "Approval recorded"
5. On error, toast shows error + overlay is cleared (mutation rollback)

**For a long-running triggered study:**

- **Visibility into progress**:
  - The `.live-hairline` (2px indicator) appears when any run is active (StudyDetail.tsx:43)
  - The lamp status flips to RUNNING (StatusStrip.tsx:8-12)
  - The metric readout on each experiment card scrambles digits every 90ms (MetricReadout:143) and locks with a green flash on new data (line 160)
  - The run table row highlights with cyan left border (styles.css:1011-1012)

- **Potential friction**:
  - 4s poll interval is too slow for a user watching a 30s compute job—consider **reducing to 2000ms** during active runs
  - The **feedback on queued state** is subtle (lamp shows ◌ QUEUED with amber pulse, but the run table shows "queued" LED at the same time—consistent, but easy to miss if you're not looking at StatusStrip)
  - There's **no "running details" modal**—you can see that a run is computing, but not its stdout/logs/resource usage. A triggered study UI might want a **side panel or collapsed details pane** showing real-time logs

- **Recommendation for triggered studies**:
  - **Keep the 4s poll** for background monitoring (battery-friendly, server-light)
  - **On manual "Run" click, temporarily boost to 2s polling** for the next 60s, then fall back to 4s (eager early feedback, then idle again)
  - **Toast should show run ID immediately** with a deeplink or auto-scroll (currently toasts are generic; line 145 says "Rerun requested — pending approval", but doesn't tell you the run ID)
  - **Add a "watching" state** in the feedback dock: replace the recommendation verb with "WATCHING RUN {id}" + a live metric scratchpad showing the primary metric as it ticks up

---

### SUMMARY TABLE: FILES & KEY LINES

| Question | File | Key Lines | Insight |
|----------|------|-----------|---------|
| **Routing** | `/src/lib/router.ts` | 1-34 | Two-route hash router; no create flow |
| **Entry Point** | `/src/components/StudyList.tsx` | 67 | Empty state directs to MCP tool, not UI |
| **API Gap** | `/src/api/client.ts` | 68-99 | No createStudy or uploadDataset method |
| **Polling** | `/src/api/hooks.ts` | 22-37 | 4s interval, stops when idle; no WebSocket |
| **Optimistic** | `/src/state/overlay.tsx` | 39-125 | Merges local actions into server data pre-confirm |
| **Live Indicator** | `/src/components/StudyDetail.tsx` | 43 | `.live-hairline` div when `computing` |
| **Lamp Status** | `/src/components/panes/StatusStrip.tsx` | 8-12 | RUNNING/QUEUED/IDLE/FLAG states |
| **Panel Layout** | `/src/styles.css` | 291-316 | 12-col grid, 2-row template; collapses on <1280px |
| **Responsive** | `/src/styles.css` | 1543-1572 | Single breakpoint at 1279px (too coarse) |
| **Empty State** | `/src/components/primitives.tsx` | 68-77 | Centered flexbox, low-contrast |
| **Dock Height** | `/src/styles.css` | 63, 1149-1157 | Fixed 104px; inflexible on mobile |
| **Feedback Form** | `/src/components/panes/Dock.tsx` | 95-145 | NL→constraint parser works; no file upload |

The cockpit is architecturally sound but operationally isolated—study creation is MCP-only, responsive design has a middle gap, and live update UX could be richer. The recommended three changes are: (1) add a create route, (2) intermediate responsive breakpoint, (3) eager polling boost on manual triggers."

### 4. LIVE UPDATE MECHANICS & TRIGGERED STUDY SURFACING

**Polling Strategy** (api/hooks.ts:22-37):

```typescript
useStudy(id): {
  refetchInterval: (query) => (hasActiveRun(query.state.data) ? 4000 : false),
}
```

- **4000ms interval** is conservative (4s between polls). For a live "triggered" study (e.g., user clicks "Run experiment"), this means **up to 4s latency** before the UI reflects the run's queued state.
- **Stops polling** once all runs exit active status (queued/running → completed/failed/stopped).
- **No WebSocket** or Server-Sent Events—purely HTTP polling.

**Optimistic Overlay** (state/overlay.tsx:1-126):

When a user clicks "Approve", the mutation:
1. Calls `api.requestApproval()` (hits the real POST)
2. **Immediately** calls `dispatch({t: 'hyp', status: 'approved'})` (optimistic)
3. Merges overlay onto StudyDetail (mergeStudyDetail:114-125), so the card flips to approved before server confirms
4. On success, shows toast "Approval recorded"
5. On error, toast shows error + overlay is cleared (mutation rollback)

- **Visibility into progress**:
  - The `.live-hairline` (2px indicator) appears when any run is active (StudyDetail.tsx:43)
  - The lamp status flips to RUNNING (StatusStrip.tsx:8-12)

  - **Keep the 4s poll** for background monitoring (battery-friendly, server-light)
  - **On manual "Run" click, temporarily boost to 2s polling** for the next 60s, then fall back to 4s (eager early feedback, then idle again)

Decisions locked in:
1. **Managed Agent is the sole driver** — flesh out `apps/agent-runtime`, bootstrap it, deploy Modal, wire trigger + SSE.
2. **Hybrid upload** — real CSV → R2 + real structural profile + Modal trains on the uploaded file, but keep a seeded leakage/critique guarantee so the demo's "caught an issue" always fires.
3. **Bigger visual redesign** of the cockpit (still professional).

The genuinely tricky architecture risk here is **streaming SSE from a Node agent-runtime through a Cloudflare Worker to the cockpit** (Workers don't hold long-lived outbound streams the way a Node process does), plus the **upload → R2 → Modal-readable URI** plumbing. Let me run a focused design pass on the three threads in parallel to pressure-test those before I commit the plan.

# Plan — Labmate end-to-end: upload + question → managed agent runs it live, with a cockpit redesign

## Context

Labmate is an agent-native data-science harness. The committed system has all the
pieces but they are **not joined up into a usable product flow**:

- You cannot start a study from the UI — the cockpit's empty state literally says
  "create one via the MCP `create_study` tool." There is no way to **upload a
  dataset** or **ask a question** in the app.
- Datasets aren't real: `create_study` takes a `dataset_id` *string* and
  `profile_dataset` returns a **canned** profile (real only for the seeded
  `sla_tickets`). R2 exists but is write-only (reports).
- The Anthropic **Managed-Agents runtime** (`apps/agent-runtime`) is fully coded and
  its smoke test passes, but **nothing triggers it**, there is **no live stream** to
  the cockpit, and it has never been bootstrapped.
- The cockpit just had a "declutter" pass; the user wants a **bigger visual
  redesign**.

This plan wires the whole loop: **a user uploads a CSV + types a question in the
cockpit → the control plane stores + profiles the data and starts a real Managed
Agent → the agent profiles, proposes, runs experiments in Modal, critiques, and
loops → the cockpit streams it live and lets the human steer → a final report.**
Plus a real cockpit redesign.

The intended architecture is already specified in `docs/GOAL_E2E.md` (the e2e
overlay); this plan executes it and adds the two pieces that overlay left open —
**real upload/profiling** and the **cockpit live view + entry screen** — at the
fidelity the user chose.

## Decisions (locked with the user)

1. **Managed Agent is the sole engine.** No deterministic fallback. Flesh out
   `apps/agent-runtime`, bootstrap it, deploy Modal, wire create → `/agent/start` →
   live SSE.
2. **Hybrid upload.** Real CSV → R2 + a real structural profile (columns, dtypes,
   missingness, row count, content hash, heuristic leakage name-scan) for any file;
   Modal trains on the uploaded file. **Keep a seeded leakage/critique guarantee** so
   the demo's "caught an issue" moment always fires.
3. **Bigger cockpit visual redesign** — a real reimagining of the visual language,
   staying professional and uncluttered (no return to CRT/grid/neon/gimmicks; see
   memory `ui-professional-restraint`).
4. **We run the deploys** — including the irreversible agent **bootstrap** (creates a
   permanent, archive-only agent). Confirm that one-way step at execution time.

## Repository logistics (do this first)

The `apps/agent-runtime/**` + e2e overlay files are **untracked** in the main
checkout and are **absent from the current worktree** (`.claude/worktrees/ui-cleanup2`,
branch `worktree-ui-cleanup2`, which holds the uncommitted UI declutter). Before
building:

- Decide one working tree. Recommended: a fresh branch off `integration` in the main
  checkout that (a) commits the untracked e2e overlay (`apps/agent-runtime`, `docs/
  GOAL_E2E.md`, `scripts/demo_e2e.mjs`, the `package.json`/`schema-check.mjs` edits)
  and (b) cherry-picks / re-applies the UI declutter from `worktree-ui-cleanup2`.
- Run `node apply-e2e.mjs` if the four shared-file edits aren't all present
  (idempotent), then `npm install` so `apps/agent-runtime` is picked up as a
  workspace. Confirm `npm run test:agent` (4 tests) passes as the baseline.

## Workstream A — Upload + real profiling (hybrid)

_(Core design finalized from the design pass — see "Design notes" below.)_

Goal: a real CSV is uploaded, stored in R2, profiled for real, fed to Modal, while
the planted "caught an issue" moment stays guaranteed.

Representative changes (control plane `apps/web`):
- **Upload + create contract.** Add the cockpit-facing create flow (multipart create
  vs. create-then-upload — finalized in design notes). New R2 key scheme
  `datasets/{study_id}/data.csv`; `dataset_id` for an uploaded study becomes its R2
  key / content hash so existing `dataset_id`-keyed code keeps working.
- **Real CSV profiler.** New module `apps/web/src/profile_csv.js`: streamed/sampled
  dtype inference (int/float/datetime/category/text), missingness, capped `n_unique`,
  and a heuristic leakage name-scan (post-outcome name regex). `profileDataset` uses
  it for uploaded datasets instead of `profileFor`; the canned `sla_tickets` profile
  stays as a recognized schema.
- **Seeded guarantee.** Preserve the planted catch via the heuristic flagging known
  post-outcome columns and/or a `constraints.banned_columns` the create form can
  preload; the runner's 422 on leaked features must stay reachable.
- **Modal-readable dataset.** A Worker route streams the R2 object so
  `manifest.dataset_uri` is fetchable; set `LABMATE_DATASET_BASE` accordingly (the
  runner already resolves `${LABMATE_DATASET_BASE}/${key}` or an http(s) URL —
  `runner.py:_load_dataset`).

## Workstream B — Trigger + live streaming (managed agent)

_(Streaming architecture finalized from the design pass — see "Design notes".)_

Goal: creating a study starts the agent; the cockpit watches live and can steer.

Representative changes:
- **Trigger.** `createStudy` (or a new `POST /api/studies/:id/start`) fires the
  runtime's `POST /agent/start` (fire-and-forget via `ctx.waitUntil`). New env
  `AGENT_RUNTIME_URL`. Runtime hosting for the demo: finalized in design notes
  (local Node process vs. Modal web endpoint).
- **Streaming.** Pick the validated approach from the design pass (direct cockpit→
  runtime SSE, Worker streaming proxy, or the `StudySession` Durable Object as an
  event hub). Implement `GET /api/studies/:id/stream` and/or the DO accordingly; the
  runtime emits structured events (`agent.activity`, `tool.use`, `tool.result`,
  `approval.needed`, `study.done`).
- **Steering + approval.** Wire the cockpit "suggest changes" box →
  `POST /agent/:id/message`; surface `request_approval` to the cockpit and unblock via
  the existing `POST /api/feedback` (type=approval), with an auto-approve-within-budget
  option for the demo.

## Workstream C — Cockpit redesign + new screens

_(Visual direction + screen specs finalized from the design pass — see "Design notes".)_

Goal: a refreshed professional visual language, a New-Study entry, and a live view.

Representative changes (`apps/cockpit`):
- **Redesign** the token system + shell per the recommended direction (keep dense
  cockpit grid vs. calmer app frame — decided in design notes), without breaking the
  working detail view.
- **New Study screen.** New route `#/create`, `CreateStudy.tsx` (file drop +
  question/brief + target/task/metric + optional banned-cols/budget), `api/client`
  `createStudy`/upload mutation + `api/hooks` `useCreateStudy`, CTA on the list view,
  navigate to `#/study/:id` on success.
- **Live view.** `useEventStream` hook over `EventSource`; render agent narration +
  tool activity into the EvidenceLedger as a live feed; a "watching run" dock state;
  coexist with the 4s react-query polling (stream = activity, poll = ledger truth);
  approval prompt surfaced inline.

## Design notes (to be filled from the design workflow)

> Pending `labmate-e2e-design` results: the recommended **streaming architecture**,
> the **upload/create contract + profiler limits + Modal-URI mechanism**, and the
> **redesign direction + concrete tokens/components**. This section will carry the
> decision-ready specifics before finalizing.

## Infra / deploy (we run these; one step is irreversible)

1. **Bootstrap the agent (IRREVERSIBLE — confirm first).** `npm run agent:bootstrap`
   creates ONE permanent agent (`claude-opus-4-8` + DS system prompt + tools + skills)
   and ONE cloud environment; writes `LABMATE_AGENT_ID` / `LABMATE_ENVIRONMENT_ID` to
   `.env`. Idempotent — reuse, never create-per-study.
2. **Deploy the Modal runner.** `modal deploy apps/modal-runner/runner.py`; set the
   web endpoint as `MODAL_RUNNER_URL` (control plane) and `LABMATE_DATASET_BASE` (so
   the runner can fetch the uploaded CSV from R2 via the Worker).
3. **Deploy the Worker.** Create D1 + R2 (`wrangler d1 create labmate`,
   `wrangler r2 bucket create labmate-artifacts`), apply `schema.sql`, set
   `LABMATE_INTERNAL_TOKEN` + `MODAL_RUNNER_URL` + `AGENT_RUNTIME_URL`, `wrangler
   deploy`.
4. **Run the agent runtime** (`npm run agent:dev` or the Modal-app variant) and point
   the cockpit at the deployed Worker (`VITE_API_BASE`, `VITE_API_TOKEN`).

## Sequencing

1. Repo consolidation + green baseline (`test:agent`).
2. A: upload + real profiling + Modal-readable dataset (Worker), with the seeded
   guarantee; unit-test the profiler.
3. B: trigger + streaming + steering (Worker + runtime); extend the smoke test.
4. Infra: bootstrap (confirm), Modal deploy, Worker deploy.
5. C: cockpit redesign + New-Study + live view.
6. E2E: one real run on the seeded study; then a real run on a freshly uploaded CSV.

## Verification

- **Unit:** `profile_csv.js` against `examples/sla_tickets/data.csv` (asserts row
  count, dtypes, missingness, and that post-outcome columns are flagged leaky).
- **Runtime:** `npm run test:agent` stays green; extend `e2e.smoke.test.mjs` to cover
  the trigger + an `approval.needed`/stream event.
- **Backend e2e (stubs where needed):** `POST /api/studies` (multipart) → study row +
  R2 object + dataset_version; `/api/studies/:id/stream` yields events; `POST
  /api/grade` → `verdict: done` (incl. `caught_an_issue`).
- **Live demo:** `npm run demo:e2e` on the seeded study runs clean twice; then drive
  the same path from the cockpit with a **freshly uploaded CSV**, watch it live,
  inject a steering message, and see the final report + model-card link.
- **Guards:** `npm run guard` green.

## Risks / watch-items

- **Managed Agents is beta** (`managed-agents-2026-04-01`); confirm exact event/tool
  shapes against the live SDK before the demo (`anthropic.mjs` is written
  defensively). Bootstrap is one-way.
- **CF Worker streaming limits** — the streaming choice must survive Worker
  constraints (the DO-hub option de-risks this; finalized in design notes).
- **Worker CPU/time on profiling** — bound the CSV profiler (sample rows, cap work).
- **Arbitrary uploaded CSVs** won't match the canned hypothesis library; the agent
  generates hypotheses for real data, but the planted self-correction is only
  guaranteed via the seeded leakage path (decision 2).

## 2. NEW STUDY screen (upload CSV + ask a question)

### Route
Add a third route to `lib/router.ts`:
```
export type Route = { name:'list' } | { name:'study'; id:string } | { name:'create' }
```
`parse`: `seg === 'create'` → `{name:'create'}`; `hrefFor` → `'#/create'`; add `navigate({name:'create'})`. `App.tsx` gains a third branch rendering `<CreateStudy/>`.

### Component: `components/CreateStudy.tsx`
A single centered card (max-width ~640px) on the list shell (reuse `.listview` padding + the new left rail). Sections:

1. **Dataset** — a drag-and-drop dropzone (`.dropzone`, dashed `--line-2`, hover/`dragover` → `--accent` border). Accepts one `.csv`. On drop/select: read `File`, show filename + size + row-estimate (count newlines client-side, cheap), and a `chip` per inferred header (parse first line). This client preview is cosmetic; the authoritative profile comes from the server.
2. **Question / brief** — a `textarea` (`brief`, required, the headline "ask a question": *"What do you want to predict, and what does success look like?"*).
3. **Target column** — a `<select>` populated from the parsed CSV headers (required). Falls back to a free-text input if no file parsed yet.
4. **Task type** — segmented control (`classification` | `regression`), drives metric defaults.
5. **Metric** — `<select>` filtered by task_type (classification: pr_auc/roc_auc/recall/precision/f1; regression: rmse/mae/r2), default sensibly; uses `METRIC_LABELS` from `derive.ts` for labels.
6. **Advanced (collapsible)** — banned columns (multi-select chips from headers, pre-checks any header matching the seeded leakage name-scan so the "caught an issue" guarantee is visible from minute one), and budget (`max_trials`, `budget_seconds` number inputs).

Reuse existing primitives/classes: `.btn`/`.btn--primary`, `.segmented`/`.seg`, `.chip`, `.label`, `.kv`. New classes: `.create`, `.dropzone`, `.dropzone.is-drag`, `.field`, `.field__error`, `.create__advanced`.

### Inline validation
Pure client checks before enabling submit: file present + `.csv` + non-empty; `brief.trim()` non-empty; `target` chosen and present in headers; `metric` set. Errors render under each field (`.field__error`, `--danger`, `aria-describedby`). Submit button disabled until valid; on 4xx from the server, surface `describeError` (already in hooks) as a top-of-form alert + toast.

### Submit flow (three-step, sequenced)
The control plane has no single create-with-file endpoint, so the mutation orchestrates:
1. `api.uploadDataset(file)` → POST the raw CSV to a **new** `/api/datasets` route (multipart or `application/octet-stream`) that stores it in R2 and returns `{ dataset_id, file_hash }`. (Backend work is outside this cockpit plan but the client method is defined here.)
2. `api.createStudy({ brief, dataset_id, target, task_type, metric, banned_columns?, budget? })` → returns `{ id }` (the worker's `createStudy`).
3. `api.startAgent(study_id)` → POST `/agent/start` (proxied through the worker or hit directly via `VITE_AGENT_BASE`) so the managed agent begins immediately. The worker's `profileDataset` runs server-side as the agent's first tool call (`profile_dataset`), so the cockpit does NOT call profile directly.

On success: `qc.invalidateQueries(['studies'])` and `navigate({name:'study', id})`. The detail view then opens straight into the live-streaming state (Section 3).

### api/client.ts additions
```
uploadDataset(file: File): Promise<{ dataset_id: string; file_hash: string }>
  // fetch(`${API_BASE}/api/datasets`, {method:'POST', body:file, headers:{authorization, 'content-type':'text/csv'}})
createStudy(body: CreateStudyInput): Promise<{ id: string } & Study>   // post('/api/studies', body)
startAgent(study_id: string): Promise<{ status: string }>
  // post to AGENT_BASE ?? API_BASE + '/agent/start'
```
Add `const AGENT_BASE = import.meta.env.VITE_AGENT_BASE ?? API_BASE`. `uploadDataset` bypasses the JSON `request()` helper (it sets `content-type: application/json` whenever there's a body) — give it its own fetch that does not JSON-stringify.

### api/hooks.ts additions
`useCreateStudy()` — a `useMutation` running the three steps above, with `onError → toast/describeError`, `onSuccess → invalidate studies + navigate`. Exposes `isPending` for the submit button.

### Where the CTA lives
On `StudyList`: a **"New study"** `.btn--primary` in `.listview__head` (next to the filter chips) and as the primary action of the empty state — replacing the current copy *"create one via the MCP create_study tool"* with a real button (`navigate({name:'create'})`). Also the brand/rail gets a persistent "+ New study" entry.

## 3. LIVE STREAMING view

### The hook: `lib/useEventStream.ts`
`useEventStream(studyId, { enabled })`:
- Opens `new EventSource(`${AGENT_BASE}/agent/${encodeURIComponent(studyId)}/stream`)` in an effect keyed on `studyId`; closes on cleanup. (EventSource can't send the bearer header; the stream route is read-only/public like the GET routes, consistent with the worker's "GET reads public".)
- Maintains `useReducer` state: `events: AgentEvent[]` (cap ~300, ring buffer), `phase` (`'connecting'|'live'|'idle'|'done'|'error'`), `pendingApproval?: {input,res}` (from `approval.needed`), `connected: boolean`.
- Maps the fixed `kind` vocabulary into typed `AgentEvent`s for the feed (`session.created`→ system line; `user.message`/`nudge`→ muted system; `agent.activity`→ narration; `tool.use`→ "calling <tool>"; `tool.result`→ result summary, error-styled if `result.error`; `human.guidance`→ your steering echoed; `approval.needed`→ sets `pendingApproval`; `study.done`/`loop.finished`→ phase `done`; `loop.error`→ phase `error`). Server already replays its buffer to late subscribers, so a refresh re-hydrates the feed.
- Returns `{ events, phase, pendingApproval, clearApproval, connected }`.

Add an `AgentEvent` discriminated union to `api/types.ts` (these are runtime SSE shapes, not OpenAPI — fine to hand-declare here with a comment, since they come from `agent-runtime`, not the spec).

### Stream vs poll coexistence (explicit contract)
- **Stream = activity** (fast, ephemeral narration; what the agent is *doing right now*). It never mutates react-query cache directly.
- **Poll/invalidate = truth** (the durable ledger: runs, critiques, decisions, dataset profile). On any `tool.result` whose tool writes server state (`profile_dataset`, `launch_experiment`, `record_critique`, `record_decision`, `write_report`), the hook fires `qc.invalidateQueries(qk.study(studyId))` so the canonical panes refresh from the worker. The existing 4s `refetchInterval` while a run is active stays as the safety net.
- This keeps `StudyDetail` + overlay semantics intact: the EvidenceLedger pane still renders `buildLedger(detail)` as the **system-of-record** timeline; the live feed is an **additive, ephemeral** strip above it.

### Rendering: EvidenceLedger becomes ledger-of-record + a live activity rail
Restructure the §04 panel into two stacked regions (no data-shape change to `buildLedger`):
1. **Live activity feed** (top, only when `phase !== 'idle'`): a compact, auto-scrolling list of `AgentEvent`s — narration in `--text-2`, tool-use rows with the tool name in mono + a spinner dot while awaiting its `tool.result`, results collapsed to one line (expand on click). Header carries the `.live-dot` + connection state. New entries use the `typein` keyframe. This is a **new** sub-component `panes/LiveFeed.tsx` consumed inside `EvidenceLedger`.
2. **Evidence ledger** (below, existing `.timeline`): unchanged — the durable, server-truth events. The `alert-pin` (the catch) stays here, driven by `methodologicalFlag(detail)`.

When `phase === 'done'`, the live feed collapses to a single "Run complete" line and the ledger is the resting state.

### Dock: a "watching run" state
`Dock`/`RecommendationDock` gains a `streamPhase` prop. While `phase==='live'`: the recommendation kicker reads **"AGENT WORKING"** with the `.live-dot`, verb shows the latest `agent.activity` summary (or "PROFILING / PROPOSING / TRAINING / CRITIQUING" inferred from the last `tool.use` name), `--accent`. Generate-report/Check-done buttons disable while live (the agent owns the loop). On `done`, dock returns to the normal recommendation/report surface.

### "Suggest changes" → steering message
The existing `FeedbackBox` stays for durable judgment (POST `/api/feedback`, unchanged). **Add a second, lighter input** in the dock or feed header: **"Suggest a change"** wired to a new `useSteerAgent(studyId)` mutation → `api.steerAgent(studyId, text)` → POST `${AGENT_BASE}/agent/:id/message {text}`. The server echoes it as a `human.guidance` event, so the steering line appears in the live feed immediately (no optimistic overlay needed — the SSE round-trips it). Disabled until `session.created` has been seen (server returns 409 `session_not_ready` otherwise — handle by disabling + tooltip).

### Approval prompt when the agent requests compute
On `approval.needed`, the hook sets `pendingApproval`. Surface it as a **prominent prompt** at the top of the live feed (and mirror as a toast): the tool input (model family, features, estimated cost) + **Approve / Deny** buttons reusing `.segmented`/`.seg--on-approve`. Approve → `actions.approve`-style call to `/api/approvals/request` (the agent's `request_approval` tool then sees the recorded approval on its next `query_runs`/dispatch and proceeds; the worker already enforces the 402-without-approval gate, so this closes the loop). `clearApproval()` after either choice. This makes the human-in-the-loop gate a real, visible interaction rather than an implicit backend rule.

## 4. Migration / sequencing (land without breaking the working detail view)

Stays as-is (data flow untouched): `StudyDetail` orchestration, `state/overlay.tsx`, `api/hooks.ts` existing mutations, `derive.ts`, `buildLedger`, `BriefPane`, `DataContractPane`, `RunTable`, `StatusStrip`, `Dock`'s feedback box, `ExperimentCards` logic. # Labmate Cockpit — Visual Redesign + Upload/Question Entry + Live Streaming

## Baseline (verified)

The worktree already carries an uncommitted "declutter" pass on top of the committed "glass cockpit": `--bg-void`, `--grid-glow`, `--scan`, the `.crt` overlay, the metric-digit scramble, the panel corner-tick "bezel screws", the card scanline sweep, and the `§NN` panel numbers / `crosshair` cursor are all gone; `--r` went 2px→5px; `MetricReadout` now holds steady while running. Two routes only (`#/`, `#/study/:id`); `Panel` lost its `num`/`crosshair` props but `ExperimentCards`/`DataContractPane` still pass them (latent TS prop mismatch to clean up). The SSE vocabulary from `loop.mjs`/`server.mjs` is fixed: `session.created`, `user.message`, `agent.activity`, `tool.use`, `tool.result`, `nudge`, `approval.needed`, `human.guidance`, `study.done`, `session.ended`, `loop.finished`, `loop.error`. The control plane exposes `createStudy({brief,dataset_id,target,metric,task_type?})` and `profileDataset({study_id})`; there is no upload route or `/agent/start` trigger from the cockpit today.

The redesign builds ON the declutter (keeps its restraint), not on the original chrome.

---

## 1. VISUAL DIRECTION

Two viable directions, then a recommendation.

### Direction A — "Refined Instrument" (evolve the current single-screen grid)
Keep the dense 12-col cockpit grid and dark field, but lift it from "avionics pastiche" to "precision instrument". Drop the Orbitron display face entirely (it's the strongest remaining gimmick) and run a single humanist UI face for all chrome, mono only for numbers/IDs/labels. Warm up the near-black, widen the type scale, soften seams from hairlines-on-near-black to a subtle two-tone surface system. Everything stays on one screen.

### Direction B — "Calm App Frame" (sidebar + content)
Move to a conventional product shell: a fixed left rail (logo, study switcher, nav: Studies / New study / the live study), a content area that swaps full views, and a right-docked "Agent" inspector for the live feed + steering. The dense grid survives only as the "overview" tab of a study; create and live-watch become first-class routed views with room to breathe. This reads more like a SaaS console and scales past the two-route hash router.

### RECOMMENDED: Direction A, with one structural borrow from B

Recommend **Direction A — Refined Instrument**, because the dense one-screen grid IS the product's identity ("watch an autonomous data scientist work on one pane of glass") and the detail view already works; a full reframe to a sidebar app (B) is a large rewrite that risks the working `StudyDetail` for little user value here. But borrow exactly one idea from B: a slim **left utility rail** on the list/create views only (brand, "New study" CTA, filters), so the create entry has an obvious home without disturbing the cockpit grid.

The redesign is a real step beyond declutter: it removes the last theme face (Orbitron), introduces a proper surface-elevation system and a wider type scale, replaces "live = animation/glow" with "live = a single quiet motion primitive + a persistent live rail", and adds two genuinely new screens.

#### Token system (drop-in replacement for `:root` in `styles.css`)

Color roles (keep the existing hues — cyan/amber/red read well on dark — but formalize roles and warm the field slightly):

```
